tags.gist: Says the competency approach extends to vision-language models, subject to two conditions drawn from an experiment on them.
Describes an experiment sending imaging prompts with no image attached to three frontier models, varying only a demographic descriptor, over 11,700 calls.
Wants benchmarks to include missing-image cases, since models diagnosed without images and abstention, the crucial behavior when scans fail to arrive, goes untested.
Says robustness and subgroup elements collapse when the image is absent, leaving the demographic descriptor driving large differences in diagnoses given.
Cautions the subgroup finding could reflect prevalence priors rather than bias, though a diagnosis without an image is indefensible either way.
Says the measurement channel matters: free text hedged while the structured diagnosis field was filled, and the schema's image indicator never contradicted a fabrication.
Reports that rephrasing prompts moved results far less than the demographic signal, so prompt sensitivity does not explain the findings.
Wants multimodal evaluation criteria to specify missing and broken-input benchmarking, subgroup consistency under them, per-channel abstention, and no reliance on self-reported input adequacy.
Notes caveats: schema enforcement and the attachment prompt are interventions, and one model's baseline diagnosis rate makes reported differences lower bounds.
